item.title: Unilorin student seeks N43m for kidney transplant
item.description: … Family spends over N20m, sells property to sustain treatment By Chioma Obinna The family of Olajide Victor, a 200-level student of the University of Ilorin, Kwara State, has appealed for N43 million to fund a kidney transplant for him after he was diagnosed with Stage V end-stage renal disease. Victor is expected to undergo the life-saving procedure at Newhaven Specialist Hospital, Lagos, as his family struggles to meet the cost of his treatment. He said his health challenges began in November 2025 after he sustained a minor fracture in his left leg while playing football at the university’s sports complex. Weeks later, his face and legs became swollen, prompting medical examinations. Following several tests, including kidney function investigations, he was diagnosed with Stage V kidney disease at Taiwo Hospital, Ilorin. A medical report signed by Dr S. Alagbe, Consultant Nephrologist, indicated that Victor requires continued haemodialysis twice weekly. His mother, Comfort Adesanya, said the family had spent over N20 million on his treatment and sold their land, house and other valuables to keep him alive. She appealed to individuals, corporate organisations and well-meaning Nigerians to help raise the N43 million required for the transplant, saying the family could no longer cope with the rising cost of treatment. Donations can be made to Victor Adekunle Olajide, UBA, Account Number: 2458216260 or call Victor on 09018866426. item.title: Food security: Nigerian farmers risk wasting billions on fertilisers without soil testing, experts warn
item.description: By Adeola Badru & Cynthia Alo Nigeria’s quest for food security may continue to suffer setbacks unless farmers move away from indiscriminate fertiliser application and embrace soil testing and crop-specific nutrient management, agricultural experts have warned. The experts, who spoke at the 2026 South-West Nigeria Fertiliser and Soil Health Summit in Ibadan, Oyo State, cautioned that increasing fertiliser consumption without understanding the specific nutrient requirements of farmland could undermine agricultural productivity, weaken farmers’ incomes and worsen soil degradation. They argued that the country’s approach to fertiliser management must go beyond distributing inputs to farmers and focus on ensuring that the right fertiliser is applied to the right soil, for the right crop and at the appropriate time. The position formed a major highlight of the communiqué issued at the end of the summit, organised by the Institute of Agricultural Research and Training (IAR&T), Obafemi Awolowo University, Moor Plantation, Ibadan, on Tuesday. With the theme, “Fertilisers and Food Security in South-West Nigeria: The Journey So Far,” the summit brought together more than 150 scientists, farmers, policymakers, fertiliser manufacturers and distributors, agricultural extension professionals and development partners to examine the challenges confronting fertiliser utilisation and soil health in the region. The participants expressed concern that the continued reliance on blanket fertiliser recommendations failed to address significant differences in soil fertility, acidity, phosphorus fixation, nutrient depletion and other soil-related challenges across different agroecological zones. According to the communiqué, “The predominance of blanket fertiliser recommendations does not adequately address the variations in soil fertility, soil acidity, phosphorus fixation, nutrient depletion and other soil constraints across different agroecological zones in the region.” The experts maintained that fertiliser recommendations should increasingly be based on soil testing, crop requirements, prevailing agroecological conditions and economically viable nutrient management practices. They also identified high fertiliser prices, inadequate distribution networks, limited access to credit and inconsistent availability as major constraints preventing smallholder farmers from accessing and effectively utilising the agricultural input. The summit further warned that declining soil organic matter, nutrient imbalance, erosion and other forms of soil degradation continued to undermine fertiliser-use efficiency and agricultural productivity. To address the situation, it called on research institutions to strengthen soil fertility mapping and develop crop-, soil- and location-specific fertiliser recommendations for major crops cultivated across South-West Nigeria. item.title: 655 tribunal registrars swear oath of secrecy ahead of 2027 election cases
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri With just 58 days to the general elections, the Court of Appeal on November 16 administered the oath of secrecy to 655 clerks and Deputy Chief Registrars selected to serve on the various election tribunals. The oath was administered under the supervision of the President of the Court of Appeal (PCA), Justice Monica Dongban-Mensem. It specifically invoked the provisions of Section 1(1) of the Official Secrets Act, which concerns the protection of official information. Under the Act, a person commits an offence if they transmit classified matter to a person to whom they are not authorised, on behalf of the Government, to transmit it. The Act also provides that a person is guilty of an offence if they obtain, reproduce, or retain classified matter which they are not authorised, on behalf of the Government, to obtain, reproduce, or retain, as the case may be. The officials were warned that the oath would remain binding even after their assignments at the tribunal ended, with the PCA vowing to hand over defaulters to security agencies for prosecution. “Is there anyone among you who did not read the oath form, or who signed it and now wants to withdraw from the assignment?” Justice Dongban-Mensem asked, as the weight of the oath dawned on the officials. “I am asking because you have just signed evidence against yourselves. Anyone we find doing what we have asked you not to do will be handed over to the Police for prosecution. “I am taking all the forms you signed to the secret registry of my office, and I will lock them in my safe. In case some of you are not aware, I began my tenure as President of this Court by handing some people over for prosecution, and they were duly prosecuted. “It is because people are not made to face the consequences of their actions that we have so many problems in this country. But at the Court of Appeal, we give you every opportunity to abide by your oath, and when you don’t, we prosecute. “Some of you may be approached and asked to give details of the tribunal members’ discussions. You will start eavesdropping to get information to pass on to them. “But when you eavesdrop, you can never get the full details. That is how, before you know it, false judgments start flying around. It often comes from the registry. “We are watching you, and many other people will be watching you too. Be very careful, be committed to the nation, and let’s get it right,” the PCA warned. Election Petition Tribunals are established to hear and determine petitions arising from the conduct of elections into political offices. Section 285(1) and (2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, empowers the President of the Court of Appeal to constitute an Election Petition Tribunal in each State of the Federation and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja. item.title: AI, fake voter records raise new risks for 2027 elections
item.description: …Why media must not rush to publish election claims —Tech players By Juliet Umeh As Nigeria prepares for the 2027 general elections, voters may face a new kind of deception. The society is now rife with images, videos and audios that appear authentic but have been fabricated or altered. The concern has grown after the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, said it removed 1,609,553 records from the voters’ register following a technical assessment. The review examined suspected multiple registrations, unusual registration patterns, substituted photographs and irregularities linked to registration transactions. INEC also found cases in which some registration personnel deliberately bypassed established procedures, including provisions for exceptional circumstances involving persons with disabilities. The commission is investigating some flagged records. The findings have prompted questions about how the irregularities occurred and whether synthetic images or other AI-generated material could be used to undermine confidence in the electoral process. There is, however, no evidence in the material available that AI-generated images caused the irregularities in the register. Olaronke Alo of the BBC Disinformation Unit while speaking on Arise Television said its initial verification found that some of the images circulating online were present in the INEC register. She said: “What we did was to do the initial verification. We went into the INEC portal and began to trace some of the names and pictures being posted on social media. We found that these images were on the INEC register.” The unit also examined claims about inconsistent records, including one instance in which the same photograph appeared against different names. Alo said it found examples of apparently incomplete or unusual names and records alleged to belong to deceased people, including former President Muhammadu Buhari. She said the unit’s task was to verify claims circulating online, rather than assess whether INEC’s response was adequate. False claims can travel fast The risks extend beyond the voters’ register. AI tools can generate convincing images, videos and audio of people appearing to say things they never said. A fabricated statement attributed to a political figure could spread rapidly before voters have time to verify it. INEC has dismissed a social media poster and accompanying text claiming the commission had reaffirmed the leadership of the African Democratic Congress. The poster carried INEC’s logo and an image of National Commissioner Mohammed Haruna. With the matter before the courts, false claims styled as official announcements could mislead the public. Other risks include political messages tailored to specific groups of voters, fabricated result sheets, screenshots purporting to show updates from INEC’s results portal, or cloned voices announcing false outcomes. item.title: Army seeks land for armoured corps training in Bauchi
item.description: …Commends Bala Mohammed for supporting military operations, infrastructure development By Christopher Ameh The Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, has appealed to the Bauchi State Government to allocate land for the establishment of a dedicated training facility for the Nigerian Army Armoured Corps in the state. Shaibu made the appeal during a courtesy visit to Governor Bala Mohammed at the Government House, Bauchi, where he commended the governor for supporting the Nigerian Army and promoting infrastructural development in the state. The Army Chief said the request had become necessary following the expansion of the Nigerian Army from eight to 12 divisions, a development that had increased the number of officers and soldiers requiring specialised training. He explained that Bauchi had remained a major training centre for armoured officers, noting that military personnel usually begin their professional careers in the state through the Young Officers’ Course and other specialised programmes. According to him, armoured officers spend more than 15 years of their military careers attending various courses in Bauchi before moving to other locations as they advance in rank. He said the proposed facility would provide a dedicated centre for the continuous training of officers and soldiers throughout the year. Shaibu disclosed that the Corps Commander of the Nigerian Army Armoured Corps would formally present the request to the governor, urging him to give it favourable consideration. “With this expansion, a lot of officers and soldiers have been coming into the Corps, and they will require this training consecutively throughout the year. Once that proposal comes, I crave your indulgence to please consider it,” he said. The Army Chief appreciated Mohammed for his administration’s support for the Armoured Corps, particularly the establishment of some military units in Alkaleri as part of efforts to expand the Army’s operational capacity. He also commended the governor’s infrastructural development efforts, describing the transformation of the Government House as remarkable. “Being an armoured officer myself and having started my career from here in Bauchi, I must acknowledge the massive infrastructural development taking place here. In fact, I did not recognise the Government House when I was coming,” he said. Shaibu further disclosed that he was in Bauchi to attend the grand finale of Exercise Mugunbugu, conducted in the Alkaleri general area. He described the exercise as the Nigerian Army’s major end-of-year training activity, designed to consolidate the various military exercises conducted throughout the year. The Army Chief also attended the maiden edition of the Nigerian Army Armoured Corps reunion and pulling-out ceremony, which attracted more than 100 retired senior officers. He said the reunion would provide an opportunity for retired officers to reflect on their contributions to the development of the Corps and share experience

item.title: Innovator develops machine to reduce drudgery in post-harvest cleaning of farm
item.description: By Cynthia Alo The use of manual methods to sort and wash agricultural produce, including tigernuts, ginger, potatoes and grains, may become less demanding with the development of a locally made machine designed to integrate sorting, washing and drying operations. The innovation, developed by a Kogi State-born physicist and innovator, Kabir Umar, is aimed at addressing the labour-intensive and often unhygienic methods used by smallholder farmers, cleaning artisans and agro-processors to prepare agricultural commodities for local consumption and processing. Umar said the absence of affordable integrated cleaning equipment had left many small-scale operators dependent on manual sorting and washing, while those seeking mechanised alternatives often had to acquire expensive imported specialised equipment. He identified tigernuts as one of the commodities particularly affected by the challenge, explaining that some cleaning artisans still use their legs to wash the nuts before sorting them by hand. According to him, similar challenges affect the handling of other agricultural commodities, including ginger, potatoes, millet, beans and hibiscus flowers, popularly known as zobo. Umar said the idea for the machine emerged in 2020 after he ventured into agro-processing and encountered difficulties with the cleaning and drying of raw agricultural materials, which he identified as an important first step in value addition. He subsequently developed a multipurpose post-harvest sorting and washing machine, with an additional drying capability, designed to provide an integrated cleaning solution for different agricultural commodities. The innovator said he had mainly used the machine to sort and wash tigernuts for further processing into tigernut flour, adding that demonstrations to tigernut cleaning artisans showed its potential to reduce manual labour and improve productivity. He, however, disclosed that the machine was still at an advanced prototype stage and had yet to be deployed sustainably to support farmers and other operators across the agricultural value chain. According to him, wider adoption of the machine could improve the quality of agricultural produce entering local markets, support value addition, create jobs and strengthen the export potential of Nigerian commodities by improving their post-harvest handling. On the challenges facing the development, Umar identified inadequate funding as a major constraint that had slowed the transition from prototype development to commercial production. He expressed optimism that intervention through the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure’s (NASENI) Innovate Naija Challenge would help accelerate the commercialisation process. item.title: Summit to examine financing, market access for farmers, agribusinesses
item.description: By Cynthia Alo Farm financing, market access and innovative solutions for farmers and agribusiness operators will take centre stage at the fifth edition of the Wealth Creation Summit scheduled for November 28, 2026, in Abuja. The summit, organised by Golden Harvest Acres Ventures, is expected to bring together more than 1,000 farmers, agribusiness owners, investors, entrepreneurs and young Nigerians to explore opportunities for improving agricultural productivity and building sustainable businesses. The event, themed, “Unlocking Opportunities for Wealth Creation, Innovation and Sustainable Agricultural Development,” will focus on connecting agricultural producers and entrepreneurs with financing opportunities, markets, investors and business development support. A major feature of the summit will be the launch of the Wealth Creation Network, an agribusiness and entrepreneurship cooperative designed to support farmers, women and young entrepreneurs through training, access to agricultural inputs, produce aggregation, market linkages and business development services. The network is also expected to provide members with opportunities for bulk produce sales, export linkages and investment-readiness training. Speaking ahead of the event, Convener of the summit and Founder of Golden Harvest Acres Ventures, Uzua Brainz, said the initiative was intended to provide participants with practical opportunities beyond conference discussions. “We do not want people to attend Wealth Creation Summit 5.0, listen to speeches and return home exactly as they came. We want them to leave with clarity, structure, connections and practical opportunities for wealth creation,” he said. item.title: Konga shows tech-enabled retail platforms can complement conventional healthcare delivery
item.description: By Prince Osuagwu The growing intersection of technology, healthcare and e-commerce is opening new opportunities for mobile health delivery in Nigeria. This is as one of Nigeria’s composite e-commerce companies Konga attracted the partnership of global skincare brand, La Roche-Posay, to expand access to dermatological expertise and authentic skincare products in the country. The partnership, leverages Konga Health’s retail and e-commerce network to connect consumers with genuine dermatological products, professional skincare advice and health education. The partnership sealed in Lagos recently, demonstrated how technology-enabled retail platforms could complement conventional healthcare delivery by making specialist skincare products and information more accessible to consumers. La Roche-Posay, a brand under L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty, partnered with Konga Health, its official distributor in Nigeria, to promote dermatological science, product authenticity and informed skincare choices. A major attraction was the interactive skin science experience, which allowed visitors to explore common skin conditions, including hyperpigmentation, acne, damaged skin barriers, dryness and the effects of ultraviolet radiation. The programme also featured free consultations with certified dermatologists and members of the L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty MedSquad, who provided professional skin analysis, guidance and practical recommendations. Among the participating specialists were Dr Ayesha Akinkugbe, dermatologist and Vice-President of the Nigerian Association of Dermatologists, and Dr Folakemi Cole-Adeife. The event showcased five major La Roche-Posay product franchises: Cicaplast for skin repair, Mela B3 for hyperpigmentation, Anthelios for sun protection, Lipikar for dry and atopic-prone skin, and Effaclar for acne-prone skin. Speaking at the event, Leo Stan Ekeh, Chairman of Zinox Group, said the commercial opportunities in Nigeria’s beauty and personal-care market, was enormous. He added that the importance of bringing globally recognised brands and quality products closer to Nigerian consumers can never be overemphasised. For Anaïs Routhiau, Business Development Manager, LID LDB SSA, the Living Lab provided an opportunity to bring La Roche-Posay’s commitment to dermatological science closer to consumers, helping them better understand their skin and the science behind the products they use. Beyond the medical engagements, the partnership addresses a growing challenge in Nigeria’s skincare market: access to genuine products and reliable health information. Through Konga Health’s distribution and e-commerce infrastructure, consumers can access authentic L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty products through an authorised channel, reducing exposure to counterfeit products and unreliable sellers. item.title: Doctors risking heart disease through overwork, sleep deprivation – Experts
item.description: … Warn of burnout, stroke risks, seek healthier work environments By Chioma Obinna Health experts yesterday expressed concerns that Nigerian medical doctors are exposing themselves to increased risks of cardiovascular diseases, including heart attacks and strokes, through excessive workloads, sleep deprivation, chronic stress and failure to undergo regular medical checks. The experts, who spoke at the Annual General Meeting/Scientific Conference of the Medical and Dental Consultants’ Association of Nigeria (MDCAN), Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Ebute-Metta, Lagos tagged: “ Your Body, Your Responsibility: A Personal Guide to Cancer Risk Reduction for Physicians, lamented that physicians, despite their knowledge of healthy living, often neglect their own health while attending to patients. They called for a deliberate shift towards preventive healthcare among doctors, warning that professional dedication should not come at the expense of their lives. Speaking at the conference, Chief Consultant Cardiologist at the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital, LASUTH, Dr Folashade Daniel, said doctors must consciously balance their professional responsibilities with adequate rest, exercise, healthy eating and routine medical examinations. Daniel, who spoke on protecting the hearts of physicians, said: “I don’t think physicians can balance their work, healthy living, and their mobility. It has to be intentional.” She noted that doctors sometimes work for extended hours, leaving little time for personal health, but stressed that they must make deliberate efforts to recover and maintain healthy lifestyles. “First of all, know that your life is not just, your life doesn’t just entail your job. You are a person, you have a family, and you have responsibilities. Yes, to your patients, but also to your family, to yourself,” she said. According to her, doctors should make adequate rest, relaxation, healthy eating and physical activity essential parts of their routines, rather than treating them as optional activities. She advised physicians with a family history of cardiovascular disease to exercise extra caution and make annual health checks a priority. “Take your birthday, for example, your one anniversary, to do a check-up. And then look up all the results with a colleague. Don’t just be your own doctors. Let somebody look at what you have, the results you have done, and give you advice as need arises,” Daniel said. The cardiologist also urged government to strengthen policies that promote healthier food choices and safer working environments. She identified excessive salt, preservatives and trans fats in food, particularly from repeatedly used frying oil, as concerns requiring stronger regulation. Daniel further recommended accessible spaces for physical activity in workplaces, including walkways, trees and encouragement for workers to use stairs where appropriate. item.title: Foursquare G.O. tasks graduands on integrity, national development
item.description: By Olayinka Latona The General Overseer of the Foursquare Gospel Church in Nigeria, Rev. Sam Aboyeji, has charged graduating students of LIFE Theological Seminary, Ikorodu, Lagos, to uphold integrity and sound biblical doctrine as they prepare to preach the Gospel and contribute to society. Aboyeji gave the charge at the institution’s 2026 graduation ceremony, where he urged the graduands to see their graduation not as an end but as a stepping stone to greater responsibilities in God’s service. Speaking on the theme of the ceremony, “Trailblazers,” and drawing from Titus 2:7-8, the cleric said the credibility of their future ministries would depend largely on the integrity of their personal lives. He said: “You have been equipped with knowledge and skills that must now find expression in faithful service to God and humanity. I charge you to distinguish yourselves as trailblazers whose lives exemplify the sound doctrine you have received.” Quoting Apostle Paul’s admonition to Titus, Aboyeji urged the graduates to be examples of good works, demonstrating integrity in doctrine, reverence, incorruptible speech and soundness of character. He warned against compromising biblical truths in the face of challenges, urging them to remain courageous, steadfast and diligent in their ministerial responsibilities. “Be courageous in breaking new ground, steadfast in the face of challenges, uncompromising in matters of biblical truth, and diligent in the discharge of your ministerial responsibilities,” he said. Reminding the graduands that service to God was a sacred responsibility requiring accountability to the Creator, the General Overseer urged them to remain worthy ambassadors of LIFE Theological Seminary and vessels of honour in their respective fields of assignment. Also speaking, the Chairman of the Governing Council of LIFE Theological Seminary, Rev. Joe Ameh, urged the graduating class to distinguish themselves as trailblazers and uncompromising ambassadors of Christ in a society increasingly challenged by moral decay and corruption. Ameh said the graduates were expected to demonstrate the values of Christianity and apply their theological training in addressing contemporary issues in a rapidly changing society. He said: “As trailblazers, those of you graduating today are expected to be ardent and passionate in distinguishing yourselves before a world characterised by normlessness and anomie. You are expected to be pathfinders in blazing the trail that should characterise the essence of being Christians with a fair measure of theological education in responding to contemporary issues in a fast-evolving setting.” The seminary council chairman also decried what he described as pervasive corrupt practices threatening the nation’s God-given assets and resources. item.title: Blindness: Eritrea, 10 others eliminate trachoma from Africa as Nigeria lags
item.description: By Sola Ogundipe Eritrea has become the 11th country in the World Health Organisation (WHO) African Region to eliminate trachoma as a public health problem, raising hopes of ending a neglected tropical disease (NTD) that continues to threaten the sight of millions of people across the continent. The achievement, validated by WHO, places Eritrea among 11 African countries that have successfully tackled the disease through sustained public health interventions, improved access to treatment, hygiene promotion and community mobilisation. Eritrea joins Algeria, Benin, Burundi, Eritrea, The Gambia, Ghana, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Senegal and Togo as the African countries that have received WHO validation as the number of countries that have achieved elimination globally stands at 34. Eritrea is also the 66th country globally and the 23rd in the WHO African Region to eliminate at least one neglected tropical disease. According to WHO, Eritrea achieved the milestone, following two decades of sustained interventions targeting the disease, particularly in remote rural communities where poor access to clean water, sanitation and healthcare had fuelled its spread. Eritrea’s success followed nationwide surveys conducted between 2006 and 2020, which helped identify affected communities and guide the rollout of interventions across the country. The government subsequently implemented WHO’s recommended SAFE strategy, a combination of surgery for advanced cases, antibiotics to clear infection, facial cleanliness to limit transmission and environmental improvements, particularly better access to water and sanitation. A notable feature of the campaign was its community-led sanitation approach, which delivered significant public health gains despite limited external funding. Health workers deployed digital tools for data collection and mapping to identify affected populations, track disease patterns and direct resources to hard-to-reach communities. In a congratulatory message, WHO Director-General, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said, “I congratulate the Government and people of Eritrea on this historic achievement. After two decades of determined effort, Eritrea has consigned trachoma as a public health problem to history. This is a victory for the communities most affected by this devastating disease, and a powerful example of what sustained national commitment can achieve.” On his part, WHO Regional Director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, said Eritrea’s achievement demonstrated the impact of political commitment, community participation and effective partnerships in tackling neglected tropical diseases. “I congratulate Eritrea on this historic public health milestone. It shows what is possible through sustained political commitment, community leadership and strong partnerships. item.title: Eyesan seeks more opportunities for women in petroleum sector
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Commission Chief Executive, Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), Mrs. Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, has called for greater opportunities for women in the petroleum sector. Eyesan made the call on Wednesday while speaking on the topic, “Breaking Barriers,” at the 2026 Women in NNPC Limited (WIN) in Abuja, under the theme, “Powered by Her.” She asked women to also prioritise competence, resilience and continuous learning as critical tools for breaking barriers. A statement by the Commission said Eyesan urged women not to be discouraged by delayed promotions, stressing that professional growth requires patience, perseverance and commitment to excellence. Sharing her personal experience, Eyesan disclosed that she spent eight years in the same position without promotion but remained committed to her career. Eyesan also emphasised the importance of involving men in conversations about gender inclusion and women’s advancement, noting that some of the major milestones in her career were made possible by men who recognised her competence and provided opportunities. “I was appointed the first female Head of Strategy, not by a woman, but by a man who believed in my competence. I was also appointed as the first female EVP Upstream, NNPCL, by a man who believed in my competence, and today I stand as the first female CCE of NUPRC by Mr President, who is a man who believes that I will deliver,” she said. Acknowledging the gradual increase in opportunities for women in the industry, the NUPRC boss called for more deliberate efforts to achieve meaningful representation, advocating at least 25 per cent participation of women in leadership and decision-making positions. “Is it happening at the scale we want? Not quite, we need more. At least one in four. Not just because we want to make up the numbers but because we think we bring value to the table,” she said. The NUPRC boss also commended the Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited, Mr Bayo Ojulari, for the WIN initiative, describing it as a valuable platform for positioning young women for greater opportunities and leadership roles in the oil and gas industry. She noted that the Nigerian oil and gas industry was recording significant progress through collaboration between the regulator, NNPC Limited and other industry operators. item.title: [VIDEO] Tinubu Can’t Alter State Police Bill, He’ll Definitely Sign It — Omole
item.description: Lawyer and author Charles Omole has said that he does not expect President Bola Tinubu to make an alteration to the National Policing Bill transmitted to him by the National Assembly. Omole, who stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday. He explained that altering the bill would return the process to the Senate, House of Representatives and state houses of assembly for their approval. Omole noted further that the constitutional amendment is not the meat and bone of policing but simply allows state police to exist, while the National Policing Bill specifies the structure and functions of the state police. He, however, said that the National Policing Bill could not be considered until the constitutional amendment had gone through. He explained that while the 36 states would have their own police service, the police in the Federal Capital Territory would be under the control of the federal police service. Omole, however, said that part of the recommendation under the bill is that states cannot buy their own arms and ammunition at will. item.title: Plateau 2027: PDP’s Scores Gov Mutfwang 15-20% In Performance
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Kephas Ropshik, on Wednesday said that Governor Caleb Mutfwang performed poorly in governance in the state. Ropshik, who spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today , said the governor had not scored more than 20 per cent in performance. The PDP candidate said that leadership should be about performance and about the people. “In fact, I can tell you on a scale of one to 100, you can give him like 15 to 20 per cent in performance,” he said. “He still remains someone that I respect, but of course that, completely, is different from politics.” ﻿ He alleged that the governor defected to the All Progressives Congress (APC) when he could not cope with the crisis in the PDP. He, however, said that the governor did not leave with up to 15 per cent of the members of the PDP, insisting that Plateau is a PDP state. “You know, a man’s strength and leadership qualities are being tested when there are crises, but the governor couldn’t stand the crisis. He left for APC, and so there was an opening in the PDP to contest for governorship because, of course, the truth is this. Plateau has been a PDP state. “You can’t take that away from Plateau State, right? And so there was a vacancy, and so somebody needed to fill in the gap. And so even with the crisis, we believed in the PDP,” the candidate said. “Mutfwang did not live with 15, 20 per cent of people, I mean, in PDP to APC. The people, in fact, not even 10 per cent, because the people that followed him to APC are his appointees, and that’s the truth. “Ninety per cent of people on the Plateau still believe in the PDP.” Ropshik said that Plateau is one of the frontrunners in the Rainbow Coalition. He also said that he was working for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu. Asked whether he was not confusing his followers by telling them to vote for the APC in the January 16 presidential election, and the PDP in the February 6, 2027 governorship election in the state, Ropshik said, “No, no, no, I am not reading because now if we want to be sincere to ourselves, the PDP presidential candidate, we all know that there’s no chance for him to win the election. “And so why should we now waste the votes? We must find a platform to identify; what we’re after is good governance.” The post Plateau 2027: PDP’s Scores Gov Mutfwang 15-20% In Performance appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: [VIDEO] Tinubu Approves Establishment Of University Of Public Relations, Leadership
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of the University of Public Relations, Leadership, the first of its kind to advance specialised education, research, professional development and leadership training in public relations. Tinubu announced this at the 13th World Public Relations Forum and the 51st Africa Public Relations Association Conference in Abuja on Wednesday. He also described it as a forward-looking investment in human capital and the future of the communication profession. The President also said it would provide an opportunity to develop a new generation of communication leaders equipped to respond to the demands of a rapidly changing global environment. “An important outcome of hosting this forum is our determination to establish a lasting institutional legacy for the public relations profession,” Tinubu, who was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima, said. “In this regard, I am pleased to formally approve and support the establishment of the University of Public Relations and Leadership.” He urged investors to explore Nigeria’s rich cultural heritage, tourism assets and the ingenuity of the Nigerian people. “ Naija no go carry last ! Nigeria is a country of enormous possibilities. We are a nation of diverse cultures, talents and ideas, with a youthful population, a dynamic private sector and a strong determination to build a more prosperous future,” he added. Watch the President’s remarks in the video below. ﻿ The post [VIDEO] Tinubu Approves Establishment Of University Of Public Relations, Leadership appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: ADC, Kaduna gov’t differ over venue
item.description: From Mohammed Ibrahim Yaba, Kaduna; Hussein Yahaya, Baba Martins & Daniel Adaji, Abuja The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the Kaduna State Government of denying the party the use of the Ranchers Bees Stadium to host the Northwest rally of its presidential campaign. The party said it had applied to use the stadium for its rally scheduled for November 17 and 18 but was refused access to the facility by the state government, which denied the claim. The ADC National Vice Chairman, North-West, Hafsat Baba, told one of our correspondents that the party dutifully informed the state government of its intention to use the facility, but the latter turned down its request. Daily Trust reports that the All Progressives Congress (APC) recently held its presidential campaign flag-off at the same venue. In a letter dated November 12, 2026 reportedly from the Kaduna State Ministry of Local Government Affairs and addressed to the Office of the National Vice Chairman of the ADC, North-West, the ministry said the stadium would not be available on the requested dates due to ongoing repairs. The letter, signed by Mohammed Sani Haruna, Senior Special Assistant to the Commissioner, stated: “We write to acknowledge receipt of your letter with the above caption. However, we regret to inform you that due to ongoing repairs at the stadium, it will not be available for the aforementioned programme on the dates requested by you.” Baba said the ADC also notified security agencies, including the Department of State Services (DSS), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Inspector-General of Police, Kaduna State Police Command and the General Officer Commanding, about the planned rally. “We sent these letters not only to state security agencies but also to their national offices, just to be on the safe side,” she said. Baba explained that the party initially considered the Ahmadu Bello Stadium but was informed that it was under construction and subsequently considered the Trade Fair Complex but was also told that the facility would not be available. She said the party decided to request Ranchers Bees Stadium after learning that the APC had recently used it for its presidential campaign flag-off. “We were aware that Ahmadu Bello Stadium was under construction. We then thought of using the Trade Fair Complex, but we were made to understand that it would also not be available. We knew that they (APC) used Ranchers Bees recently, so we decided to request it, but it was denied,” she said. The ADC chieftain questioned why its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, should be prevented from holding a rally in Kaduna, which she described as his second home. “If Atiku can visit Bauchi and Yobe and hold his rallies, why can’t he come to Kaduna, his second home, because he has a house here?” she asked. The development comes weeks after President Bola Tinubu flagged off the APC’s 2027 presidential campaign in Kaduna on October 24 at the same stadium. Also speaking, the ADC
